title: Collection of Rosicrucian and Alchemical Texts (PH255)
shelf_note: An 18th-century Latin manuscript of alchemical processes (antimony regulus, 'Mercurii mediante Arsenico nostro praeparatio', 'Explicatio dubiorum ... super hoc Regulo', a citation of Philaletha) belongs on an alchemy/Rosicrucian shelf; tradition field is null and no collections are given in the packet.
structure_note: No structure counts in the packet. None of the three pages has a translation, so a reader gets only the transcription. Pages 78, 154 and 232 are each a single verso in the same hand; nothing suggests a splice or a wrong work.

book_verdict: Right leaves and a well-photographed, legible manuscript, but the transcription does not handle the alchemical symbols: they are dropped, read as words ('et', 'gum', 'jam'), or expanded wrongly (nitre and salt as 'O[lei]'). Doses and two key statements are reversed ('non' for 'nostrum', 'absque purificatione' for 'atque purificatur'), the facing leaf's edge is read as a column, and no page has a translation. An expert would flag it on sight.
